stem.text: Telomerase is an enzyme that prevents the shortening of telomeres. It is **not** present in most normal cells, but is active in an estimated 85% to 95% of human tumour cells.
Which statement explains the effect of telomerase on human tumour cells?

A.text: Telomerase triggers a self-destruct process, known as apoptosis, ending the life of the cell.

B.text: Telomerase damages the chromosomes so they become genetically unstable and are unable to replicate and divide.

C.text: Telomerase helps human tumour cells avoid senescence, or cell death, which is usually the expected consequence of repeated cell division.

D.text: Telomerase enables the human tumour cells to divide more rapidly by reducing the time taken for a complete mitotic cell cycle.
